# Movie dataset initial exploration

[link to the description online](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/ggplot2movies/movies.html)

The data contains:
- 58,788 movies (rows)
  
```{r initial exploration}
movies <- movies
head(movies)
dim(movies)
```

```{r summary plots & cleaning}
movies |> drop_na("budget") |> nrow() # 5215 of 58788, thus remove column unless interested in budget
# mpaa is not present for all, thus it is not a useful variable and removed

min(movies$year)
max(movies$year)

sum(is.na(movies$year))
sum(is.na(movies$rating))

clean_movies <- movies |> 
  select(-budget, -mpaa) |> 
  mutate(genre = factor(case_when(rowSums(pick(Action:Romance)) > 1 ~ 0,
                           Action == 1 ~ 1,
                           Animation == 1 ~ 2,
                           Comedy == 1 ~ 3,
                           Drama == 1 ~ 4,
                           Documentary == 1 ~ 5,
                           Romance == 1 ~ 6)))

genre_levels <- c("NA", "0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6")

genre_labels <- c(
  "Unknown",
  "Crosslisted",
  "Action",
  "Animation",
  "Comedy",
  "Drama",
  "Documentary",
  "Romance"
  )

genre_colors <- c(
  "grey",
  "chartreuse4",
  "gold",
  "blue",
  "orange",
  "mediumpurple",
  "hotpink",
  "violetred4"
  )

table(factor(clean_movies$genre))  # basic table

genre_table <- clean_movies |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Genre representation of movies on IMDB"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c("Action", "Animation", "Comedy",
                "Drama", "Documentary", "Romance"), 
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Data from ggplot2's movies dataset.",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  )

genre_table

# code for table with the help of rbloggers to make it pretty: https://www.r-bloggers.com/2024/10/table-it-like-a-pro-print-ready-tables-in-r/
```




```{r}
plot1 <- clean_movies|> 
  mutate(genre = fct_na_value_to_level(
      factor(genre, levels = genre_levels),
      level = "NA")) |>
  filter(votes >= 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = rating, color = genre, fill = genre)) + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(breaks = genre_levels, 
                    labels = genre_labels,
                    values = genre_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(breaks = genre_levels, 
                    labels = genre_labels,
                    values = genre_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(11890, 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, 1940,1950,1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1:10)) +
  theme_minimal()

plot1
```


```{r}
plot2 <- clean_movies|> 
  mutate(genre = fct_na_value_to_level(
      factor(genre, levels = genre_levels),
      level = "NA")) |>
  filter(votes >= 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, fill = genre)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, ) +
  scale_fill_manual(breaks = genre_levels, 
                    labels = genre_labels,
                    values = genre_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1895, 1905, 1915, 1925, 1935, 1945,1955,1965, 1975, 1985, 1995, 2005)) +
  theme_minimal()

plot2
```

# Linear Model: Rating ~ Genre
*Significant effects: *
*Assumptions: Homoscedascity of Residual Variance seems to be provided, as well as a normal distribution*
```{r lm}
fit <- lm(rating ~ genre, data = clean_movies)
summary(fit)
plot(fit)
```
